all_known: D support width zero, causal logical width and randomization radius generally nonzero; no claim both potential scores become observed
all_missing: support D bounds [-4,4], finite causal support [-4,4], confidence [-4,4]; complete-case means/differences undefined and omitted, never filled zero
assignment: conditional on observed arm counts, independent uniform fixed-count assignment within each college; counts must be floor/ceiling half as generator specifies; odd-college coin is conditioned on
causal_assumptions: two well-defined full measured reference scores for every randomized person regardless of subsequent enrollment or response
consistency and no interference between people
original college-block offer assignment faithfully recorded; no postassignment selection of randomized roster
fixed potential scores under the stated reference measurement regime; outcome support 1..5
causal_logical_bounds: For each assigned1 person, potential difference in [person_L-5,person_U-1]; assigned0 in [1-person_U,5-person_L]. Average across all N. These bound the finite potential-score effect itself with no probabilistic use of randomization. Endpoints attainable on the score grid; not confidence limits.
complete_case: pooled and college-standardized complete-score arm differences describe selected observed groups, not identified causal effects; omit a mean/difference if any necessary subset has no full score, with explicit defined flag
confidence: r=sqrt(Vmax/alpha). By unbiasedness, Neyman variance formula and Chebyshev, [D-r,D+r] covers fixed finite causal effect with probability >=1-alpha over original randomization conditional on counts. Observed support bounds contain D for every valid missingness pattern, so report [max(-4,D_lower-r),min(4,D_upper+r)]. This procedure is conservative, finite-sample and does not assume a response model. It is a randomization confidence statement, not a posterior probability or a conditional-on-this-realized-assignment coverage statement. No simulated coverage claim.
display: counts integer; score means and limits 6 decimals; fractions percent one decimal; CSV values 17 digits
example_selection: first sorted randomized ID with 12-month survey returned, exactly one blank wellbeing item, and an observed wb4 different from 3; not chosen by arm contrast or result
exclusions: hidden complete items or paired item potential-score benchmarks
latent trajectory effects as measured score truth
effect of uptake rather than offer
permutation test of a sharp null
failures: nonrespondent incorrectly included in randomized file
invalid offer/binary flags or college joins
assignment counts not balanced within a college
raw item outside blank or exact 1..5
wave nonresponse with recorded item values
invalid alpha, empty group, singleton college, nonfinite arithmetic
missingness_assumption: none for support bounds or the expanded randomization confidence procedure; no MAR or equal-response-rate inference
patterns: three wave-response bits in 3,6,12 order; intermittent return means a 1 after an earlier 0; includes 001,010,011,101; monotone patterns 000,100,110,111
realized_contrast: D=sum_c (N_c/N)*(mean_full_assigned1_c-mean_full_assigned0_c). This is a randomization estimator, not exact causal truth for one assignment. Bound each arm with all retained item information. lower=sum w*(L_c1-U_c0); upper=sum w*(U_c1-L_c0).
reference_source: Liu and Yang (2020), Biometrika 107(4),935-948; arXiv:1908.01628v2, Section 2 Proposition 1 for exact full-data mean/variance. Range bound plus Chebyshev expansion derived here; no normal approximation or estimated complete-case variance used.
score: complete score only when all five raw items are known, reverse wb4; otherwise blank; record sum of every observed keyed cell and [sum+missing,sum+5*missing]/5 person limits
target: finite randomized-roster average of 12-month offer versus no-offer potential five-item wellbeing scores; equal-person, equivalently college N_c/N weighting
variance_derivation: With full outcomes, Var(D | counts)=sum_c w_c^2*(S_c1^2/n_c1 + S_c0^2/n_c0 - S_ctau^2/N_c), finite variances use denominator N_c-1. Score range four gives S_cz^2<=4*N_c/(N_c-1). Drop nonnegative effect-variance term; Vmax=4*sum_c w_c^2*N_c/(N_c-1)*(1/n_c1+1/n_c0).
